questions.question: Responsive typography means font sizes:

options.text: Scale appropriately across device sizes (not fixed px everywhere)

questions.explanation: Type should adapt to viewport for readability — via media queries, clamp(), or fluid techniques.

questions.question: clamp(1rem, 0.5rem + 1vw, 1.5rem) gives a font size that:

options.text: Is never below 1rem nor above 1.5rem, fluid in between

questions.explanation: clamp(min, preferred, max): the preferred (viewport-based) value is used, bounded by min and max — fluid type without media queries.

questions.question: rem is relative to:
questions.explanation: rem = root em (html font-size). em = parent's font-size. Using rem keeps scaling predictable from the root.

questions.question: em can be tricky because it is relative to:

options.text: The font-size of the element's parent (compounding in nested contexts)

questions.explanation: em references the parent font-size; nested em values compound, which is why rem is often preferred for consistent scaling.

questions.question: Setting html { font-size: 62.5% } is a trick to:

options.text: Make 1rem ≈ 10px so rem math is easier (10px base)

questions.explanation: 62.5% of 16px = 10px, so 1.6rem = 16px. A common convenience (though some prefer leaving 16px base).

questions.question: A modular scale helps by:

options.text: Defining harmonious font-size ratios (e.g. 1.25) across heading levels

questions.explanation: A ratio-based scale produces consistent, pleasing type hierarchy rather than arbitrary sizes.

questions.question: Line-length (measure) best practice is roughly:

options.text: 45-75 characters per line for comfortable reading

questions.explanation: Optimal measure ~45-75 chars; too wide or narrow harms readability. Constrain paragraph max-width accordingly.

questions.question: Viewport-relative units for type include:
questions.explanation: vw scales with viewport width; often combined with clamp()/calc() to avoid extremes on very small/large screens.
